review.why: The PR removes the explicit 404 check for missing posts in DELETE /posts/<id>, causing a 500 Internal Server Error when trying to delete a non-existent post instead of the documented 404 response, because accessing post.author on None raises an AttributeError.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing the explicit 404 abort causes db.session.get to return None, then accessing post.author raises AttributeError, resulting in a 500 error instead of the intended 404 for missing posts.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR introduces a regression: deleting a non-existent post now returns 500 instead of 404 because the missing-post check was removed without adding a guard before accessing post.author.

suspicions.claim: DELETE /posts/<id> returns 500 Internal Server Error instead of 404 when the post does not exist
suspicions.trigger: Send DELETE /api/posts/999999 with a valid Authorization: Bearer <token> header; read back the HTTP status code and JSON error body.
suspicions.evidence: DELETE /api/posts/999999 returned 404 in base and 500 in head, matching the suspected regression.
